This is a well-structured, accessible HTML5 document demonstrating modern best practices for semantic markup and inclusive design.

It uses semantic landmarks, a skip link for keyboard navigation, and CSS that adapts to your light or dark mode preference.

Text and link colors meet WCAG AA contrast in both themes, type scales with your browser's font size, and motion respects your system settings.

Features

  • Semantic HTML structure with proper landmarks
  • Keyboard accessible navigation and focus management
  • Dark mode support with custom color schemes
  • Responsive typography using modern CSS
  • Print-friendly styles for better readability
  • WCAG AA contrast compliance in all color modes

Examples

Component Cards

Card components are useful for organizing related content. They include a subtle border and padding for visual separation.

Learn more about accessibility resources

Interactive Elements

Buttons and links are fully accessible with clear focus states. All interactive elements include visible focus indicators and proper ARIA labels.

Keyboard navigation: Use Tab to move forward, Shift+Tab to move backward, and Enter to activate.

Accessible Form

Fields marked * are required.

For example, name@example.com

Live Region Example

Click the button to announce a message using a live region. This demonstrates how screen readers are notified of dynamic updates.

Resources

Want to learn more about web accessibility and semantic HTML? Check out these resources:

  • WCAG 2.2 Quick Reference (opens in new tab)
  • HTML Living Standard (opens in new tab)
  • A11y 101 (opens in new tab)
  • Back to top

content.text:
`0.html` was already well built, with accessible landmarks, contrast, dark mode, reduced-motion and print support. So I made five small fixes instead of rewriting it. I haven't opened it in a browser to check the changes.

1. **External-link arrow:** links that open in a new tab now show a small ↗ after the text. Before, only screen reader users were told the link opens a new tab. The arrow is marked so screen readers skip it, which avoids announcing it twice. When printing, the existing rule that prints the link's URL takes its place.
2. **No stuck hover on touch screens:** hover effects on links and buttons now only apply on devices that can actually hover. On phones they used to stay "on" after a tap. The thicker underline still shows while a link is being pressed.
3. **Keyboard shortcut markup:** `Shift+Tab` is now marked up as two separate keys (`<kbd><kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd></kbd>`), which is the standard way to mark up a key combination. New CSS keeps it looking like a single key badge.
4. **Message length limit:** the message box now has a 2,000-character limit and a hint below it saying so. The hint is linked to the field so screen readers read it out.
5. **Tidy-up:** I removed a leftover style from the button hover rule that did nothing.

`0.html` was already well built, with accessible landmarks, contrast, dark mode, reduced-motion and print support. So I made five small fixes instead of rewriting it. I haven't opened it in a browser to check the changes.

1. **External-link arrow:** links that open in a new tab now show a small ↗ after the text. Before, only screen reader users were told the link opens a new tab. The arrow is marked so screen readers skip it, which avoids announcing it twice. When printing, the existing rule that prints the link's URL takes its place.
2. **No stuck hover on touch screens:** hover effects on links and buttons now only apply on devices that can actually hover. On phones they used to stay "on" after a tap. The thicker underline still shows while a link is being pressed.
3. **Keyboard shortcut markup:** `Shift+Tab` is now marked up as two separate keys (`<kbd><kbd>Shift</kbd>+<kbd>Tab</kbd></kbd>`), which is the standard way to mark up a key combination. New CSS keeps it looking like a single key badge.
4. **Message length limit:** the message box now has a 2,000-character limit and a hint below it saying so. The hint is linked to the field so screen readers read it out.
5. **Tidy-up:** I removed a leftover style from the button hover rule that did nothing.
